batches.exam: Assistant Director (Food & Drugs), November-2025 · General English, Section B (66 MCQs)
batches.evidence: Printed pages 3-9 of the Nov-2025 CDPO/Assistant Director (Food & Drugs) General English booklet read page by page against the stored stems, option order and shared directions; printed underlines of Q1-10, Q21-26 and Q44-46 and the (a)-(d) labels of Q44-46 were checked visually, and every item was solved independently before comparison with the provisional answer key (No. Asst. Director (C)/25/2025-MPSC(Exam)(1), dated 11 Nov 2025), page 1, "General English" table, whose 66 cells were read cell by cell. 64 answers match the key; Q8 (independent: conjunction; key: D preposition) and Q19 (both (a) over and (d) above fit; key: D above) are held unscored by the guide adapter. Section A written prompts remain pending source review.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: There is a party next week __though__ I don’t think I can go.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “though” joins the two clauses “There is a party next week” and “I don’t think I can go”, so it is a subordinating conjunction. A preposition would have to take a noun object, and neither an adverb nor an adjective can link two clauses here. → (b) Conjunction.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: She is __very__ uninclined to read the manuscript.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “very” modifies the adjective “uninclined” (“She is very uninclined”), and a word that qualifies an adjective is an adverb. → (b) Adverb.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: __Well__, I don’t know about that.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “Well” stands on its own before the sentence as an exclamation of hesitation; a word used like that is an interjection. → (c) Interjection.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: __What__ a piece of work is man!
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: In the exclamatory “What a piece of work is man!”, “What” introduces and qualifies the noun phrase “a piece of work”, so it is used adjectivally (as a determiner before a noun). → (c) Adjective.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: He proclaimed his __love__ for Estella in front of everyone.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “love” is the object of “proclaimed” — the thing he proclaimed — so it names a thing here and is a noun, not the verb of the sentence. → (a) Noun.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: I do not simply __love__, you, I worship and adore you.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “love” is the finite verb of “I do not simply love”, set against “worship and adore”; a word that states the subject’s action is a verb. → (b) Verb.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: Puia __himself__ stood up and spoke in favour of the proposal, but it was of no use.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “himself” points back to the subject “Puia” (Puia himself stood up), so it is the emphatic/reflexive pronoun. → (d) Pronoun.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: He had joined the office two years __before__ his father died.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “before” is followed by the complete clause “his father died” (subject + finite verb), which makes it a subordinating conjunction; used as a preposition it would take a noun complement (“before his father’s death”). The provisional key marks (d) Preposition, so this item is held unscored as a key conflict.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: I won’t leave __until__ you are ready.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “until” introduces the clause “you are ready” (subject + finite verb), so here it is a subordinating conjunction. → (a) Conjunction.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: I __wish__ I had a million dollars.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “wish” is the main predicate of “I wish I had a million dollars”, attributing a state to the subject, so it is a verb. → (a) Verb.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: Go, and run ______; we shall call you when it is time to come in.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The reply “we shall call you when it is time to come in” shows the child is being sent off to play: “run about” means to move about out of doors. “run in / across / on” do not give that sense. → (b) about.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: Many years ______, I met a man who told me my fortune.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “Many years ago” is the standard marker of a finished past time; “ago” counts back from now and is not used with “since” or “hence” in this pattern. → (c) ago.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: The examination will commence ______6th November.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: Days and dates take the preposition “on”: the exam begins “on 6th November”. → (b) on.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: He is late;______, we shall start without him.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The second clause gives the result of the first — he is late, therefore we start without him. “consequently” is the only result-linking adverb offered; “whereas” and “provided” introduce clauses and “finally” marks sequence. → (c) consequently.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: I had no time to warn you. ______, I wasn’t sure.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “besides” adds a further independent reason: I had no time to warn you; in addition, I was not sure. “beside” is a preposition meaning “next to”, and “aside/asides” cannot serve as the sentence adverb here. → (a) besides.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: Do this in accordance _______ the directions you have received.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The fixed collocation is “in accordance with”. → (d) with.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: We must treat everyone equally, irrespective _____ race, class or gender.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The fixed collocation is “irrespective of”. → (d) of.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: I shall be back _____ 11:00 a.m. today.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: A deadline stated as a clock time takes “by” — not later than 11:00 a.m. “in 11:00” and “on 11:00” are not used this way, and “within” needs a period (“within an hour”). → (c) by.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: He swore upon the sky ______ his head that he will not betray me.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The blank needs a word meaning “directly above his head”. Both (a) over and (d) above complete the printed sentence idiomatically (“the sky over/above his head”), while (b) on and (c) upon would repeat the earlier “upon” and misplace the sky. The provisional key marks (d) above; because more than one printed choice is defensible, the item is held unscored as ambiguous rather than forced to the key.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: The man died ____ cholera, leaving behind his wife and two children.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: Death from a disease takes “of”: “died of cholera”. “die from” is normally reserved for wounds or external injury, and “by/with” do not collocate with a disease. → (b) of.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: She refused to believe __that he could win the tournament.__
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “that he could win the tournament” is the object of the verb “believe” (she refused to believe [what?]), so it is a noun clause. → (a) Noun clause.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: To err is human, but __to forgive__ is divine.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “to forgive” is the subject of “is divine” (To forgive is divine). An infinitive used as a subject is a noun phrase; it contains no finite verb, so it cannot be a clause. → (c) Noun phrase.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: The book __that you gave me__ was fascinating.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “that you gave me” qualifies the noun “book” (which book?), so it is an adjective (relative) clause. → (d) Adjective clause.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: The man __wearing a red hat__ is my uncle.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “wearing a red hat” is a participial phrase that modifies “the man”, so it functions adjectivally; with no finite verb inside it is a phrase, not a clause. → (c) Adjective phrase.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: Tell me __what happened yesterday__ .
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “what happened yesterday” is the object of “tell” (Tell me [what?]) — a clause doing the work of a noun, i.e. a noun clause. → (a) Noun Clause.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: She took time off __for a much needed vacation__.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “for a much needed vacation” is a prepositional phrase answering why she took time off. A phrase that modifies the verb of the sentence is an adverb phrase. → (a) Adverb phrase.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: I was not at all sure of your success. (to Affirmative)
expectedOptions: I was sure of your success
I was doubtful of your success
I was at all sure of your success
I was unenthusiastic of your success
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “not at all sure” means the same as “doubtful”, so the affirmative rendering is “I was doubtful of your success”. Option (a) reverses the meaning, and (c) is ungrammatical because “at all” requires the negative. → (b) I was doubtful of your success.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: O that I may see her again! (to Assertive)
expectedOptions: O I wish that I may see her again.
That I may see her again.
I wonder if I will see her again.
I wish that I may see her again.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The optative “O that I may see her again!” expresses a wish, and its assertive form is “I wish that I may see her again”. Option (a) wrongly keeps the exclamation “O”. → (d) I wish that I may see her again.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: How can I bear it any longer? (to Assertive)
expectedOptions: I can bear it no longer
It is asked if I can bear it any longer
I would not bear it no longer
It is too hard to bear
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The rhetorical question “How can I bear it any longer?” asserts inability, so the assertive form is “I can bear it no longer”. Option (b) is still a question and (c) carries a double negative. → (a) I can bear it no longer.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: It is possible that I may have been mistaken. (to Negative)
expectedOptions: It is not possible that I may have been mistaken
It is possible that I may have not been mistaken
It is impossible that I may have been mistaken
It is not impossible that I may have been mistaken
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The negative must keep the original sense: “possible” negated without reversing it is “not impossible”. Options (a) and (c) reverse the meaning and (b) places the negative on the wrong word. → (d) It is not impossible that I may have been mistaken.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: It is sad that children are the victims of war. (to Exclamatory)
expectedOptions: Alas! that children are the victims of war!
Pooh! That children are the victims of war!
O that children may be the victims of war!
What victims of war children are!
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “It is sad that …” becomes the exclamatory “Alas! that …”, because “Alas” is the interjection of sorrow and the clause is left intact. Option (d) restates the fact instead of the sadness. → (a) Alas! that children are the victims of war!

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: The maid said, “The boy was hiding in a closet.” (to Indirect)
expectedOptions: The maid said that the boy was hiding in a closet.
The maid said that the boy hid in a closet
The maid said that the boy had been hiding in a closet.
The maid said that the boy had hid in a closet.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: In reported speech the past continuous “was hiding” moves one step back to the past perfect continuous “had been hiding”; the reporting clause and the rest of the quotation stay as printed. → (c) The maid said that the boy had been hiding in a closet.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: He told me that he had not seen Mary since the previous day. (to Direct)
expectedOptions: He told me, “I had not seen Mary since the previous day.”
He said to me, “I have not seen Mary since yesterday.”
He tells to me “I had not seen Mary since the previous day.”
He said, “He had not seen Mary since the previous day.”
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: Changing back to direct speech: “told me” becomes “said to me”, the past perfect “had not seen” returns to “have not seen”, and “the previous day” returns to the word actually spoken, “yesterday”. → (b) He said to me, “I have not seen Mary since yesterday.”

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: She said to Peter, “Give me your book, please” (to Indirect)
expectedOptions: She said to Peter that give her his book please.
She requested Peter to give her his book.
She told Peter to give her his book please.
She asked Peter to give me your book.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: A request marked by “please” is reported with “requested … to”: “She requested Peter to give her his book”. Option (a) is ungrammatical, (c) leaves “please” inside the reported clause and (d) mixes up the persons. → (b) She requested Peter to give her his book.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: The teacher said that the earth revolves around the sun. (to Direct)
expectedOptions: The teacher said, “The earth revolves around the sun.”
The teacher said, “the earth revolved around the sun.”
The teacher says, “The earth revolve around the sun.”
The teacher said, “The earth has revolved around the sun.”
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: A universal truth is not backshifted in reported speech, so the direct form keeps the present simple: “The earth revolves around the sun”. → (a) The teacher said, “The earth revolves around the sun.”

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: Siami said, “Rama called me up this morning.” (to Indirect)
expectedOptions: Siami said that Rama called me up this morning.
Siami said that Rama called her up this morning.
Siami said that Rama called her up that morning.
Siami said that Rama had called her up that morning.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: Reported speech changes the pronoun “me” to “her”, the time word “this morning” to “that morning”, and the simple past “called” to the past perfect “had called”. → (d) Siami said that Rama had called her up that morning.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: He is a _______, therefore, he never drinks.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: A teetotaler is a person who never drinks alcohol, which is exactly what “therefore, he never drinks” needs. “totalitarian” is a political system, and “teeter-totter” and “tattle-tale” are unrelated. → (a) teetotaler.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: He has been found ________ for this post due to canvassing.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: Being disqualified for canvassing means being found not eligible: “ineligible”. “indelible” means permanent, “inedible” means uneatable and “intelligible” means understandable. → (a) ineligible.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: In a ________ gesture, she donated the prize money to charity.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: Giving away the prize money is a generous act, and “magnanimous” means generous, especially towards someone who has less. “bellicose” is warlike, “voluminous” large and “maleficient” harmful. → (c) magnanimous.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: Jack was the _______ of elegance and class.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The set idiom is “the epitome of X” — the perfect example of X. An “epigram” is a witty saying, an “epilogue” a closing section and the “epicenter” is the point on the ground above an earthquake. → (b) epitome.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: The country was a ______, ruled by a queen.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: A state ruled by a queen is a monarchy. “matrilineal” describes descent through the mother rather than a state, “matricide” is killing one’s own mother and “matrimony” is marriage. → (d) monarchy.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: He is a(n) _______ who hates anyone practicing a different religion.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: A person who hates anyone practising a different religion is a bigot — intolerant of other people’s beliefs. An atheist does not believe in God, a racist discriminates by race and an infidel is a non-believer in the speaker’s own faith. → (c) bigot.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: You must consult only _______ sources for your research.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: Research must use sources that can be relied on: “credible” means believable or trustworthy. “incredible” and “inconceivable” mean the opposite, while “conceivable” merely means thinkable. → (a) credible.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: __I enjoyed__ / __during my__ / __stay in England.__ / __No error__ .
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “enjoy” is a transitive verb taking a noun or gerund as its object (“I enjoyed my stay” / “I enjoyed staying”), so it cannot be completed by the prepositional phrase “during my …”. The fault lies in part (a); parts (b) and (c) are well formed. → (a) I enjoyed.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: __They appointed__ / __him as a manager__ /__as he is efficient.__ /__No error.__
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: After “appoint”, the post is named by a bare singular noun: “They appointed him manager”. The article “a” and “as” in part (b) break that construction, while parts (a) and (c) read correctly. → (b) him as a manager.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: __Mr. Sharma is planning__ /__to settle in Delhi__ / __as soon as he will retire in Apil next year.__ /__No error__
expectedOptions: as soon as he will retire in Apil next year.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: In a time clause introduced by “as soon as”, the verb must be simple present, not “will” + base form: “… as soon as he retires”. Part (c) therefore carries the error (and it is the printed segment that also prints “Apil”). → (c) as soon as he will retire in Apil next year.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: We _____ (drive) all the way to the resort, only for it to be closed.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The narrative sits in the past and “only for it to be closed” continues it, so the simple past “drove” is required. → (c) drove.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: It ______ (rain) when he came over this morning.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The rain was already in progress at the moment “he came over this morning”, which calls for the past continuous “was raining”. → (d) was raining.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: She _____ (work) in this office since 2000.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “since 2000” runs up to the present with the action still continuing, which calls for the present perfect continuous “has been working”. → (c) has been working.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: The teacher ______ (want) to see you immediately.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: A general statement about the teacher takes the simple present third person “wants”. The stative verb “want” is not used in the continuous (“is wanting”), and “want/wanted” do not fit the present-tense statement. → (a) wants.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: You must _____ (complete) this assignment today itself.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “must” is a modal auxiliary and is followed by the bare infinitive: “must complete”. → (b) complete.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: I ______ (wear) a white dress on my wedding day.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The wedding is a planned future event expressed as a simple intention, so “will wear” fits; “will have worn” would need a finished reference point (e.g. “by then”) and “will worn” is not a possible form. → (b) will wear.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: She _____ (sit) there waiting for you for over an hour.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The sitting began earlier and is still going on for a stated duration (“for over an hour”), which calls for the present perfect continuous “has been sitting”. → (c) has been sitting.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: She _____ (go) for a walk every evening.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: A routine repeated every evening takes the simple present, third person singular: “She goes for a walk every evening.” → (b) goes.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: I _____ (hope) for a promotion at work this year.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The speaker is currently expecting a promotion this year, so the present continuous “am hoping” is the natural form; “hoped” clashes with the present expectation and “will hope” is not used this way. → (a) am hoping.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: He ______ (prefer) his wife to stay at home.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “prefer” is a stative verb used in the simple present, so “He prefers …” is correct; continuous forms (“is preferring”) are not used for it. → (c) prefers.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: The triangles are congruent; _______ they are equal.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: Congruence of the triangles is the reason and their equality the consequence, so a result connector is needed: “hence”. “but” and “still” contrast the clauses and “otherwise” states a condition. → (b) hence.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: In an unjust society, the corrupt prosper _____ the honest stay poor.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The two clauses are set in contrast — the corrupt prosper while the honest stay poor — so the contrastive connector “while” is required. → (a) while.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: I shall do it ________ you asked me to.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “since” gives the reason for doing it: because you asked me to. “when” and “before” clash with the past tense of “asked”, and “so that” needs a purpose clause containing a modal. → (d) since.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: You may have a cookie ______ you finish your vegetables first.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: The cookie is allowed on condition that the vegetables are finished first: “provided” (= provided that) states that condition. “unless” would reverse it, and “though/until” give no condition at all. → (a) provided.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: I shall help him _______ he does not deserve it.
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: Helping him is set against his not deserving it — that is concession, expressed by “though”. “if” would make the help depend on his not deserving it, and “for/since” would offer it as the reason for helping. → (a) though.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: A lone wolf
expectedOptions: one who prefers to live alone
one who casts the deciding vote
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: A lone wolf is a person who prefers to live and act alone. → (c) one who prefers to live alone.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: A rule of thumb
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: A rule of thumb is a rough, practical estimate or method used instead of a precise calculation or rule. → (a) A rough estimate or measurement.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: To be close-fisted
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “close-fisted” describes someone unwilling to part with money — miserly. → (d) To be miserly.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: Up to one’s elbows
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: “Up to one’s elbows (in something)” means being deeply involved or absorbed in it. → (a) Deeply involved in something.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.expectedQuestion: To hold one’s tongue
mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-assistant.explanation: To hold one’s tongue is to keep silent and refrain from saying what one might say. → (b) To keep silent.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-inspector.expectedQuestion: This is **what** I want.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-inspector.expectedQuestion: The player **kicked** the ball.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-inspector.expectedQuestion: These mangoes are **almost** ripe.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-inspector.expectedQuestion: She swam ______ the river to the other side.

mpsc-group-b-archive-lang-2025-inspector.expectedQuestion: His head is teeming ___________ brilliant ideas.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q51.expectedQuestion: Three ropes of lengths 15 m, 20 m and 25 m are cut into equal pieces of maximum length. What is the length of each piece?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q51.explanation: The maximum equal piece length is the HCF: 15 = 3×5, 20 = 2²×5, 25 = 5², so HCF(15, 20, 25) = 5 m, giving 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 pieces.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q52.expectedQuestion: A number is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net change?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q52.explanation: Successive factors multiply: 1.20 × 0.80 = 0.96, so the number falls to 96% of itself — a 4% decrease. (Equivalently −20²/100 = −4%.) 'No change' is the classic trap.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q54.expectedQuestion: The average rainfall for the three months from January to March is 12 cm, and for the four months from March to June is 18 cm. If the average rainfall for the six months from January to June is 16 cm, what is the rainfall in the month of March?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q54.explanation: Jan–Mar sums to 3×12 = 36 and Mar–Jun to 4×18 = 72; adding these counts March twice, so 36 + 72 = (Jan–Jun total) + March = 6×16 + March = 96 + March, giving March = 12 cm.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q55.expectedQuestion: In an examination, 80% of the students pass in Paper I and 70% pass in Paper II. If 15% of the students fail in both Paper I and Paper II, and the number of students who pass in both papers is 520, what is the total number of students who appeared in the examination?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q55.explanation: 15% fail both, so 85% pass at least one. By inclusion-exclusion, both = 80% + 70% − 85% = 65%. Then 0.65 × T = 520, so T = 800 — consistent with the marked option.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q56.expectedQuestion: If a : b = 4 : 7 and b : c = 3 : 5, find a : b : c
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q56.explanation: Make b common: multiply the first ratio by 3 and the second by 7, giving a : b = 12 : 21 and b : c = 21 : 35, hence a : b : c = 12 : 21 : 35.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q57.expectedQuestion: A sum of money is divided among A, B, and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. If C receives ₹ 200 more than B, what is the total sum of money?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q57.explanation: Let the parts be 2x, 3x, 5x. C − B = 5x − 3x = 2x = 200, so x = 100 and the total 10x = ₹1,000.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q58.expectedQuestion: A man sells two articles for ₹ 100 each. On one he gains 20% and on the other he loses 20%. What is his overall result?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q58.explanation: Cost prices are 100/1.2 = ₹83.33 and 100/0.8 = ₹125, totalling ₹208.33 against ₹200 received — a loss of ₹8.33, i.e. 4%. Equal-percentage gain and loss on the same selling price always gives a loss of x²/100 = 4%.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q59.expectedQuestion: A can complete a work in 12 days and B can complete it in 6 days. In how many days will they complete the work together?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q59.explanation: Combined one-day work = 1/12 + 1/6 = 1/12 + 2/12 = 3/12 = 1/4, so the job takes 4 days.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q60.expectedQuestion: Pipe A can fill a tank in 15 hours and Pipe B can empty it in 20 hours. If both are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q60.explanation: Net filling per hour = 1/15 − 1/20 = (4 − 3)/60 = 1/60 of the tank, so it fills in 60 hours.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q63.explanation: Downstream speed = 30/2 = 15 km/h, upstream = 30/3 = 10 km/h. Still-water speed is their mean, (15 + 10)/2 = 12.5 km/h (the stream is 2.5 km/h).

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q64.expectedQuestion: A circular field has a radius of 7 m. A footpath of width 7 m is constructed outside it. Find the area of the footpath.
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q64.explanation: The path is the annulus between radii 14 m and 7 m: area = π(14² − 7²) = (22/7)(196 − 49) = (22/7)(147) = 462 m². Option (c), 616 m², is the whole outer circle — the trap.

A cuboid of dimensions 12 cm × 10 cm × 8 cm is melted to form cubes of side 4 cm. How many such cubes can be formed?
Options:
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q65.explanation: Cuboid volume = 12 × 10 × 8 = 960 cm³; each cube is 4³ = 64 cm³; 960 ÷ 64 = 15 exactly, so the count is a whole number and 15 cubes are formed.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q66.expectedQuestion: A square floor has dimensions 40 ft × 40 ft. Tiles of area 4 sq ft are used. If the cost of each tile is ₹ 200, what is the total expenditure?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q66.explanation: Floor area = 1,600 sq ft; number of tiles = 1600/4 = 400; cost = 400 × 200 = ₹80,000.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q67.expectedQuestion: The total of the ages of Dinga, Hminga and Liana is 80 years. What was the total of their ages three years ago?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q67.explanation: Each of the three was 3 years younger, so the total drops by 3 × 3 = 9: 80 − 9 = 71 years. Subtracting only 3 (giving 77) is the standard trap.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q70.explanation: Walking towards each other, the relative speed is 5 + 10 = 15 m/min, so the 1,200 m gap closes in 1200/15 = 80 minutes.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q059.explanation: For the AP, a=7, d=4, and aₙ=139. Thus n=(139−7)/4+1=34 terms (A).

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q060.expectedQuestion: The cost of a Cell phone is ₹27,000. A customer agrees to make a down payment of ₹7,260 and the remaining to be paid in two equal annual instalments of ₹11,374 each. The total interest paid is-
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q060.explanation: After ₹7,260 down, principal financed=27,000−7,260=₹19,740. Total installments=2×11,374=₹22,748, so interest=22,748−19,740=₹3,008 (B).

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q061.expectedQuestion: A sum of money becomes ₹2,000 in 2 years and ₹2,100 in 3 years. If the interest is compounded annually, the rate of interest charged per annum is-
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q061.explanation: For annual compounding, A₃/A₂=1+r. Hence 2100/2000=1+r, giving r=0.05=5% (B).

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q062.expectedQuestion: On a horizontal ground, a boy walks 34m due North and turns to right and walks 24m due East. From the East he again walks 27m towards South. How far is he now from the starting point?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q062.explanation: Net displacement is 7 m north (34−27) and 24 m east. Distance=√(7²+24²)=25 m (D).

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q063.expectedQuestion: There are two wires of length 44cm each. One wire is bent to form a square and the other wire is also bent to form a circle. With this information, which of the following statements is true?
expectedOptions: Data inadequate to find their areas
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q063.explanation: Square perimeter 44 gives side 11 and area 121 cm². Circle circumference 44 gives radius 22/π and area 484/π≈154 cm², so the circle encloses more area (A).

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q001.expectedQuestion: Which of the following is a characteristic of SSDs (Solid State Drives)?
expectedOptions: They are more durable and faster
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q001.explanation: An SSD (Solid State Drive) stores data in flash memory and has no moving parts, so it is more resistant to shock (more durable) and its read/write access is faster than a mechanical HDD. Option (a) “moving parts” and (d) “magnetic storage” describe an HDD, and (b) reverses the speed comparison.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q002.expectedQuestion: What technology is primarily associated with the third generation of computers?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q002.explanation: Computer generations are named by their main electronic component: 1st vacuum tubes, 2nd transistors, 3rd integrated circuits (ICs), 4th microprocessors. The third generation therefore used Integrated Circuits.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q003.expectedQuestion: Devices used by banking industry to read account numbers on cheques
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q003.explanation: MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) reads the magnetic-ink characters printed along the bottom of a cheque, which encode the bank, branch and account number; banks use it for fast, accurate cheque processing.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q004.expectedQuestion: A computer program that is designed to run a computer's hardware and application programs is called -
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q004.explanation: System software — the operating system and device drivers — is designed to run the computer's hardware and provides the platform on which application programs run. Application software performs user tasks, while database and utility software are specific kinds of program.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q005.expectedQuestion: Which of the following is a type of computer memory built directly into the processor or CPU (Central Processing Unit) that is used to store and manipulate data during the execution of instructions -
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q005.explanation: Registers are small, very fast storage locations built directly into the CPU. The processor loads operands into registers and manipulates them there while executing instructions. Cache is fast memory near the CPU, but the registers are the storage the CPU works on directly.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q006.expectedQuestion: What is a "widget" in GUI terminology?
expectedOptions: A command used in a shell
A graphical control element, like a button or slider
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q006.explanation: In GUI terminology a widget (a control) is a reusable graphical element the user interacts with, such as a button, checkbox, radio button or slider.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q007.expectedQuestion: What is the primary purpose of an I/O system in a computer?
expectedOptions: To increase the processing power of the CPU
To facilitate communication between the computer and external devices
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q007.explanation: The input/output (I/O) system manages the transfer of data between the computer (CPU and memory) and external devices such as the keyboard, display, disk and printer. It does not itself store data permanently or add processing power.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q008.expectedQuestion: In GUI design, what does "responsive design" refer to?
expectedOptions: A design that reacts to user input
A design that uses minimal graphics
A design that adapts to different screen sizes and resolutions
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q008.explanation: Responsive design builds a layout that adapts to different screen sizes and resolutions, so the same page stays usable on a phone, tablet and desktop.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q036.expectedQuestion: What least number must be subtracted from 518, so that the difference is completely divisible by 13?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q036.explanation: 13 × 39 = 507 and 13 × 40 = 520, so 518 is 11 above 507. Subtracting 11 gives 507 = 13 × 39 exactly. The least number to subtract is 11.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q038.expectedQuestion: What will be the average of the first 5 positive even numbers divisible by 9?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q038.explanation: Numbers that are positive, even and divisible by 9 are the multiples of 18: 18, 36, 54, 72, 90. Their average is 270 ÷ 5 = 54.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q039.expectedQuestion: A man buys 400 oranges for ₹2000. How many oranges can be sold for ₹260 so that he gets a profit of 30%?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q039.explanation: Cost price per orange = ₹2000 ÷ 400 = ₹5. A 30% profit needs a selling price of ₹5 × 1.30 = ₹6.50 per orange. At ₹260, the number of oranges = 260 ÷ 6.50 = 40.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q040.expectedQuestion: A and B can together complete a work in 3 days. They started together but after 2 days, B left the work. If the work is completed after 2 more days, B alone could do the work in how many days?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q040.explanation: A and B together do 1/3 of the work per day. In the first 2 days they finish 2/3, leaving 1/3 that A does alone over the next 2 days, so A's rate is 1/6 per day. B's rate = 1/3 − 1/6 = 1/6, so B alone needs 6 days.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q041.expectedQuestion: For a certain sum, the simple interest in 2 years at 8% per annum is ₹110 more than the simple interest in 1 year at the rate of 5% per annum for the same sum. Find the sum.
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q041.explanation: Let the sum be P. Interest at 8% for 2 years = 0.16P; at 5% for 1 year = 0.05P. Difference = 0.16P − 0.05P = 0.11P = ₹110, so P = ₹1000.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q042.expectedQuestion: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from two points which are at distances of 10m and 5m from the base of the tower, and in the same side and same straight line with it are complementary. The height of the tower is
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q042.explanation: Let h be the height. From 10 m, tan θ = h/10; from 5 m the angle is complementary, so tan(90° − θ) = h/5. Since tan θ × tan(90° − θ) = 1, (h/10)(h/5) = 1, giving h² = 50 and h = √50 m.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q043.expectedQuestion: What is the sum of first 30 natural numbers?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q043.explanation: Sum of the first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2. For n = 30: 30 × 31 / 2 = 465.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q045.expectedQuestion: A student has to score 40% marks to get through the exam. If he gets 40 marks and fails by 40 marks, then find the maximum marks set for the examination.
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q045.explanation: Passing marks needed = marks scored (40) + marks short (40) = 80, which is 40% of the maximum. Maximum marks = 80 ÷ 0.40 = 200.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q056.expectedQuestion: If (-5)^(x + 1) × (-5)^4 = (-5)^8, then the value of x is -
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q056.explanation: The bases are equal, so add the exponents: (x + 1) + 4 = 8. Thus x + 5 = 8 and x = 3, option (b). This independently derived result matches the MPSC final key.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q064.expectedQuestion: In tossing two coins, the probability of getting a head is -
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q064.explanation: Two fair coins have outcomes HH, HT, TH, TT. Exactly one head gives 2/4=1/2; at least one head gives 3/4. Since the printed stem only says “getting a head,” it does not specify which event; the official final key marks this question “Compensated.”
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q064.holdReason: The question is ambiguous between exactly one head and at least one head; official key compensates it. Do not assign a single answer.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q065.expectedQuestion: A survey shows that 64% of a group of people like tea, whereas 46% like coffee. What percentage of the people like both tea and coffee?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q065.explanation: The key gives 10% using 64%+46%−100%. This is the minimum possible overlap: inclusion–exclusion only implies overlap ≥10%; it can be as high as 46% if some people like neither. Since the stem does not say everyone likes at least one, 10% is conditional on that unstated assumption; item held as ambiguous.
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q065.holdReason: Official key is D/10%, but the stem never says all people like tea or coffee; overlap can range from 10% to 46%. Hold pending resolution of the missing union assumption.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q067.expectedQuestion: ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ. Which letter in this alphabet is the eighth letter to the right of the letter and which is tenth letter to the left of the last but one letter of the alphabet?

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q068.expectedQuestion: How many pairs of letters are there in the word "CASTRAPHONE" which have as many letters between them in the word as in the alphabet?

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q069.expectedQuestion: A dice is numbered from 1 to 6 in different ways. If 1 is adjacent to 2, 4 and 6, then which of the following statements is necessarily true?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q069.explanation: A face on a cube is adjacent to four faces and opposite one. Since 1 is adjacent to 2, 4 and 6, the remaining 3/5 relationship forced by the possible dice arrangements is adjacency, option C.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q070.expectedQuestion: Today is Monday. After 61 days, it will be:
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q070.explanation: 61 days is 8 weeks plus 5 days. Monday + 5 days = Saturday, option D.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q071.expectedQuestion: In an election between two candidates, one got 55% of the total valid votes, 20% of the votes were invalid. If the total number of votes was 7500, the number of valid votes that the other candidate got, was:
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q071.explanation: Valid votes = 80% × 7500 = 6000. The other candidate received 45% of valid votes: 0.45 × 6000 = 2700, option B.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q072.expectedQuestion: Which word does NOT belong with the others?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q072.explanation: Parsley, basil and dill are herbs; mayonnaise is a condiment, option D.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q074.explanation: A cup is associated with a lip as a bird is with its beak, option D.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q075.expectedQuestion: Which one will replace the question mark?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q075.explanation: In each fork, the bottom number is one-tenth of the sum of the three top numbers: (12+18+30)/10=6; (16+24+40)/10=8; (45+18+27)/10=9. Option C.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q076.expectedQuestion: One morning Udai and Vishal were talking to each other face to face at a crossing. If Vishal's shadow was exactly to the left of Udai, which direction was Udai facing?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q076.explanation: In the morning the Sun is east, so a person’s shadow points west. West is on the left when facing north; Udai faces north, option C.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q077.expectedQuestion: If South-East becomes North, North-East becomes West and so on. What will West become?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q077.explanation: The stated compass remapping advances each direction by 225° clockwise (SE→N and NE→W). West therefore maps to South-East, option C.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q078.expectedQuestion: Identify the figure that completes the pattern.
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q078.explanation: Match the line endpoints that continue across the blank cell’s borders in the 2×2 pattern. Only figure 4 completes those continuations, option D.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q079.expectedQuestion: Identify the figure that completes the pattern.
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q079.explanation: The left column uses the triangle-symbol group and the right column uses the diamond-symbol group; the missing lower-right cell must continue the diamond arrangement. Figure 4, option D.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q080.expectedQuestion: Select a suitable figure from the four alternatives that would complete the figure matrix
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q080.explanation: Within each row, the middle cell combines the line elements in the left and right cells. In the last row, removing the curved line leaves the X in option 4, so D.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q081.expectedQuestion: The school principal has received complaints from parents about bullying in the school yard during recess. Which situation should the recess aides report? i. A girl sits alone reading. ii. Four girls surround another girl and seem to have her backpack. iii. Two boys argue during basketball. iv. Three boys play a prohibited handheld video game.
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q081.explanation: Only case (ii) describes a likely bullying incident: a group surrounding one child and taking the child’s backpack. Loneliness, a sports argument and a rule violation alone do not establish bullying; option B.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q082.expectedQuestion: Severe drought is reported in several parts of the country. Courses of action: I. Government should immediately arrange financial assistance for those affected. II. Food, water and fodder should immediately be sent to save people and cattle. Which course follows?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q082.explanation: Sending food, water and fodder directly addresses the immediate drought emergency (II). The statement does not establish that financial assistance is the immediate necessary action (I), so only II follows, option B.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q083.expectedQuestion: A alone can do a piece of work in 6 days and B alone in 8 days. A and B undertook to do it for Rs. 3200. With the help of C, they completed the work in 3 days. How much is to be paid to C?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q083.explanation: A and B together complete 7/24 of the job per day. Since the job takes 3 days with C, the combined rate is 1/3; C contributes 1/3−7/24=1/24 per day. In three days C contributes 1/8 of the work, hence 1/8×₹3200=₹400, option B.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q091.expectedQuestion: How many triangles are there in the figure below?

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q092.expectedQuestion: Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a circle facing one another. P is opposite Q. Q is to the right of T and left of R. P is to the left of U and right of S. Who is opposite S?

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q093.expectedQuestion: Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a circle facing one another. P is opposite Q. Q is to the right of T and left of R. P is to the left of U and right of S. Who sits between P and R?

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q094.expectedQuestion: Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a circle facing one another. P is opposite Q. Q is to the right of T and left of R. P is to the left of U and right of S. If P and R exchange positions, who sits between S and U?

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q095.expectedQuestion: By looking in a mirror, it appears that it is 6:30 in the clock. What is the real time?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q095.explanation: For a standard clock, mirror time is obtained by subtracting from 11:60. 11:60 − 6:30 = 5:30.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q096.expectedQuestion: What is the angle between the hour hand and minute hand when the clock shows 8:30 pm?
mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q096.explanation: The minute hand is at 180°. The hour hand is at 8 × 30° + 30 × 0.5° = 255°. Their smaller angle is 75°.

mpsc-group-b-ng-2024-paper-2-a-q098.expectedQuestion: If hockey is called football, football is called badminton, badminton is called cricket, cricket is called tennis, tennis is called squash, and squash is called hockey, with which game is Lallianzuala Chhangte associated?

7, 11, 15, …, 215

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q81.expectedQuestion: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term: String : Sitar :: Percussion : ?

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q82.expectedQuestion:
Choose the word which has the same relationship among the three given words:
Cricket, Hockey, Football
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q82.explanation: Cricket, hockey and football are all outdoor team sports played on a field, and kabaddi is the only option that shares all three features. Tennis and swimming are essentially individual, and chess is an indoor board game.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q83.expectedQuestion:

(i) Relief, (ii) Warning, (iii) Flood, (iv) Rescue, (v) Rehabilitation

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q84.explanation: The terms are 2!, 3!, 4!, 5!, so the next is 6! = 720. Read as multipliers it is the same thing: ×3, ×4, ×5, then ×6 gives 120 × 6 = 720.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q85.expectedQuestion: If ‘he will say’ is coded as ‘1 3 9’ and ‘say to him’ is coded as ‘3 5 2’ and ‘he may do’ is coded as ‘8 7 9’, then what will be the code of ‘will’?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q85.explanation: The first and second statements share only 'say' and only the digit 3, so say = 3; the first and third share only 'he' and only the digit 9, so he = 9. That leaves 1 for 'will'.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q86.expectedQuestion: How many meaningful English words can be made from ‘RTEA’ using each letter once?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q86.explanation: Using all four letters exactly once gives RATE, TEAR and TARE — three words. The count depends on accepting TARE (the weight of an empty container), which is a standard dictionary word.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q87.expectedQuestion:
If ‘P’ means ‘×’, ‘Q’ means ‘÷’, ‘R’ means ‘+’, ‘S’ means ‘−’, then
18 Q 3 P 4 R 5 S 6 = ?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q87.explanation: Substituting gives 18 ÷ 3 × 4 + 5 − 6. By BODMAS, division and multiplication go left to right: 18 ÷ 3 = 6, 6 × 4 = 24, then 24 + 5 − 6 = 23.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q88.expectedQuestion: In a row of boys, Liana is 12th from the left and 15th from the right. How many boys are there in the row?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q88.explanation: Total = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1 = 12 + 15 − 1 = 26, subtracting 1 because Liana is counted in both positions.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q89.expectedQuestion:
Find the missing character:
A 3-row by 3-column table of numbers. Top row: 9, 16, 25. Middle row: 3, 4, 5. Bottom row: 12, 20, ? (the question mark occupies the bottom-right cell).
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q89.explanation: Two consistent rules give the same value. Row 1 = (Row 2)²: 3²=9, 4²=16, 5²=25; and Row 3 = Row 1 + Row 2: 9+3=12, 16+4=20, so 25+5 = 30. Equivalently Row 3 = n(n+1): 3·4=12, 4·5=20, 5·6 = 30.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q90.expectedQuestion:
How many triangles are there in the given figure?
A staircase of three right triangles above a large triangle. Three vertical lines V1 (leftmost), V2 (middle) and V3 (rightmost) all run down to a common horizontal base line; V1 is the tallest, V2 shorter, V3 shortest, their tops stepping down and to the right. From the top of each vertical a hypotenuse runs down-left at roughly 45 degrees. Triangle 1: from the top of V1 the hypotenuse falls to the left end of a short horizontal H1, which runs right to meet V1. Triangle 2: from the top of V2 the hypotenuse falls to the left end of horizontal H2, which runs right to V2; this hypotenuse passes exactly through the point where H1 meets V1. Triangle 3: from the top of V3 a long diagonal falls down-left, crossing V2 at the right-hand end of H2 and crossing V1 at the left-hand end of horizontal H3 (H3 runs right from V1 to V3), and continues all the way down to the left-hand end of the base line. Finally, from the right-hand end of the base line a slanted side rises up-left to the point where H3 meets the top of V3, closing the large bottom triangle on its right. The outer left and right slants do not meet each other, so no single all-enclosing triangle exists.
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q90.explanation: Modelling the eleven drawn segments and enumerating every triple that meets in three distinct points gives 10 triangles: the three staircase right triangles, the sub-triangle each of the second and third staircase hypotenuses cuts off on the vertical to its left, the triangle the long diagonal cuts on the third horizontal, the three triangles the long diagonal makes with the base and each of the three verticals, and the right-hand triangle formed by the base, the third vertical and the right slant. Confidence is medium because the count depends on reading the long diagonal as passing exactly through the corner where the middle horizontal meets the middle vertical.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q91.expectedQuestion:
A piece of paper is folded and cut as shown below in the question figures. How would this paper look when unfolded?
Three question figures. (1) A square with a dashed horizontal crease about 31% down from the top and a downward arrow: the top strip is folded down. (2) The resulting wide rectangle (the folded-away strip shown dotted above it) with a dashed vertical crease about 31% in from the left and a rightward arrow: the left strip is folded to the right. (3) The resulting small square (folded-away parts shown dotted to its left and above) containing two small circular punches, one near its top-left corner and one near its bottom-right corner. The four answer figures are squares showing (a) a 2×2 block of four circles in the upper-left, (b) four circles in a loose diamond in the upper-right area, (c) three circles — two diagonal near the top-left and one at the bottom-right, and (d) five circles — a 2×2 block of four in the upper-left plus one at the bottom-right.
expectedOptions: A square with four small circles arranged in a 2×2 block in the upper-left area.
A square with four small circles: one near the top, two side by side below it, and one below-left of those.
A square with three small circles: two near the top-left set diagonally, and one near the bottom-right.
A square with five small circles: a 2×2 block of four in the upper-left area plus one near the bottom-right.
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q91.explanation: Fold 1 brings the top strip (about 31% of the height) down, and fold 2 brings the left strip (about 31% of the width) rightwards, so the remaining square has a 4-layer top-left region, two 2-layer regions and a 1-layer bottom-right region. The punch in the top-left sits over 4 layers and opens out as a 2×2 block of holes, while the punch at the bottom-right sits over a single layer and stays one hole — five holes in that exact arrangement, which is only option (d).

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q92.expectedQuestion: If today is a Monday, after 75 days it will be:
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q92.explanation: 75 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 5 (70 days are exactly 10 weeks), so the day advances five places from Monday: Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat — Saturday.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q93.expectedQuestion: One sunny morning, Mawii walks towards the east and saw her friend Liana coming from a certain direction. Mawii recognizes that Liana’s shadow is directly on his left side. From which direction is Liana approaching from?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q93.explanation: In the morning the sun is in the east, so every shadow falls towards the west. For Liana's shadow to lie on Liana's left, Liana must be facing north, which means she is walking northwards and therefore approaching from the south. Confidence is medium only because the pronoun 'his' is ambiguous — read as Mawii's left it would put a shadow to the north, which is impossible in the morning, so the Liana reading is the only coherent one.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q94.expectedQuestion:
Choose the odd one out from the given figures:
Four bracketed 2×2 arrangements of arrows. (a) top row up, down; bottom row down, up. (b) top row up, down; bottom row up, down. (c) top row right, left; bottom row left, right. (d) top row left, right; bottom row right, left.
expectedOptions: Top row: up-arrow, down-arrow; bottom row: down-arrow, up-arrow.
Top row: up-arrow, down-arrow; bottom row: up-arrow, down-arrow.

Top row: left-arrow, right-arrow; bottom row: right-arrow, left-arrow.
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q94.explanation: In (a), (c) and (d) the bottom row is the reverse of the top row, so the arrows match along the diagonals and each figure is unchanged by a 180° turn. In (b) the bottom row simply repeats the top row, so each column carries the same arrow — that is the odd one out.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q95.expectedQuestion:
In the following figure, what should replace the question mark?
A box divided into four blocks, each block having a top row of three letters and a bottom row of three numbers. Block 1: letters A B C over numbers 1, 2, 3. Block 2: letters D E F over numbers 1, 4, 9. Block 3: letters G H I over numbers 1, 16, 81. Block 4: letters J K L over numbers 1, ?, 6561.
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q95.explanation: Each block holds the letters and, below them, powers of 1, 2 and 3: ABC gives 1¹, 2¹, 3¹ = 1, 2, 3; DEF gives 1², 2², 3² = 1, 4, 9; GHI gives 1⁴, 2⁴, 3⁴ = 1, 16, 81; so JKL must give 1⁸, 2⁸, 3⁸ = 1, 256, 6561 (and 3⁸ = 6561 confirms the exponent). The missing value is 2⁸ = 256.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q96.expectedQuestion:
Statements:
All fruits are flowers.
All seeds are fruits.
Conclusions:
I. All flowers are fruits.
II. All seeds are flowers.
Select the best option from the following:
expectedOptions: If both Conclusions I and II follow.
If neither Conclusions I nor II follows.
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q96.explanation: Seeds ⊆ fruits ⊆ flowers, so all seeds are flowers and Conclusion II follows. Conclusion I is the illicit converse of 'all fruits are flowers' — the flower set may be larger — so only II follows.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q97.expectedQuestion: Six friends are sitting in a row. Puia sits exactly in between Sanga and Vula. Nunga sits exactly in between Lawma and Thanga. Five friends sit to the left of Sanga. Thanga is not sitting immediately next to Vula. Who sits second to the left of Vula?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q97.explanation: Five friends to Sanga's left fixes Sanga at seat 6, and Puia between Sanga and Vula forces Vula 4, Puia 5. Nunga between Lawma and Thanga takes seat 2 with the other two at 1 and 3, and since Thanga cannot be next to Vula, seat 3 is Lawma and seat 1 Thanga; the row is Thanga, Nunga, Lawma, Vula, Puia, Sanga, so two seats left of Vula is Nunga.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q98.expectedQuestion: In a certain code language, LOVE is written as MUWI and GOOD is written as HUUE. How will KIND be written in the same language?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q98.explanation: Consonants move one letter forward (L→M, V→W, G→H, D→E) while vowels move to the next vowel (O→U, E→I). Applying this to KIND: K→L, I→O, N→O, D→E, giving LOOE.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q99.expectedQuestion: If the letters of the word REASONING are arranged in alphabetical order, how many letters will remain in the same position?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q99.explanation: REASONING sorts to AEGINNORS. Comparing position by position — R/A, E/E, A/G, S/I, O/N, N/N, I/O, N/R, G/S — only positions 2 (E) and 6 (N) match, so 2 letters stay put.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q100.expectedQuestion: T is the daughter of S whose wife is R. R is the daughter of P whose husband is Q. How is S related to P?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q100.explanation: S is male (R is described as S's wife) and R is P's daughter, so S is the husband of P's daughter — P's son-in-law. T is P's granddaughter and Q is P's husband, neither of which changes S's relation.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q80.expectedQuestion: A clock is set right at 6 AM. If the clock gains 12 minutes in 24 hours, what will be the right time when the clock indicates 12 Noon on the following day?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q80.explanation: From 6 AM to 12 noon the next day the clock shows 30 hours = 1800 clock-minutes, and 1452 clock-minutes correspond to 1440 true minutes, so true elapsed time = 1800 × 1440/1452 = 1785.12 min = 29 h 45 min 07 s; the right time is 11:45:07 AM. That value is not printed, and 11:48 AM is nearer to it (2 min 53 s away) than 11:42 AM (3 min 07 s away), so I take (c) while flagging the question as defective.
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q80.holdReason: Defective/voided: correct time is about 11:45:07 AM; no option matches, and the final key marks it Compensated.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q82.expectedQuestion:
Choose the correct image as the rotated image of the given image, when the image is rotated in the specified direction and through the angle mentioned:
A square divided into four equal quadrants, with a curved arrow above it labelled 180°. Top-left quadrant: a 'V' shape drawn as two line segments meeting at a lower vertex, with small open circles at all three ends (two at the top, one at the bottom vertex). Top-right quadrant: parallel diagonal hatching lines running lower-left to upper-right ('/' direction). Bottom-left quadrant: the same '/' diagonal hatching. Bottom-right quadrant: a diamond (square rotated 45°) with a vertical and a horizontal line crossing inside it. The four answer figures are: (A) top-left '/' hatching, top-right a sideways three-circle 'V' opening left, bottom-left diamond-with-cross, bottom-right '/' hatching. (B) top-left '/' hatching, top-right an upright three-circle 'V', bottom-left diamond-with-cross, bottom-right '/' hatching. (C) top-left diamond-with-cross, top-right '/' hatching, bottom-left '/' hatching, bottom-right an upright three-circle 'V'. Study the following questions carefully and choose the right answer:
1. Curd    2. Grass    3. Butter    4.Milk    5.Cow

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q85.expectedQuestion: There are five brothers — Suman, Kiran, Mohan, Aaron and Rajan. Mohan is the tallest. Suman is shorter than Kiran but taller than Rajan. Aaron is a little shorter than Kiran and a little taller than Suman. Who is the shortest?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q85.explanation: Mohan is tallest; Kiran > Aaron > Suman from the third clue, and Suman > Rajan from the second. The full order is Mohan > Kiran > Aaron > Suman > Rajan, so Rajan is shortest.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q86.explanation: The relation is synonymy: vacant means empty, and dearth means scarcity. 'Abundant' is the antonym trap.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q87.expectedQuestion: One morning Udai and Vishal were talking to each other face to face at a crossing. If Vishal's shadow was exactly to the left of Udai, which direction was Udai facing?
mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q87.explanation: In the morning the sun is in the east, so all shadows fall to the west. The shadow lies to Udai's left, so west is on Udai's left — and a person facing north has west on their left. Udai therefore faces North.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q88.explanation: The first letters run S, T, U, V, W (+1 each); the second letters run C, E, G, I, K (+2 each); the third letters run D, F, H, J, L (+2 each). The missing term is therefore VIJ.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q89.expectedQuestion:
Find the next figure that completes the given sequence:
A left-to-right series of three block arrows pointing right, each containing a row of seven circles, followed by a question mark. Figure 1: circle 1 shaded, circles 2–7 open; one vertical arrow above the body pointing up and one below pointing down, both at the left end. Figure 2: circles 1 and 3 shaded; two arrows above (first pointing down, second pointing up) and two below (first pointing up, second pointing down). Figure 3: circles 1, 3 and 5 shaded; three arrows above (down, down, up) and three below (up, up, down). Answer figures, each a right-pointing block arrow with seven circles: (A) circles 1, 3, 5 shaded; four arrows above all pointing down and four below all pointing up. (B) circles 1, 3, 5, 7 shaded; four arrows above pointing down, up, down, up and four below pointing up, down, up, down. (C) circles 1, 3, 5, 7 shaded; four arrows above all pointing up and four below all pointing down. The seven circles gain one shaded circle each step at alternate positions: 1 shaded, then 1 and 3, then 1, 3 and 5, so next comes 1, 3, 5 and 7 — four shaded. Only (D) has both four shaded circles and that arrow pattern; (A) has only three shaded circles.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q90.expectedQuestion: If in a certain language NATURE is coded as MASUQE, how is FAMINE coded in that code?

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q91.explanation: The Equator and the Tropic of Cancer are both particular lines of latitude, so three of the four terms belong to the latitude family. Longitude, which measures east–west position, is the odd one.

mpsc-group-b-co-2026-p2-Q92.explanation: Every letter of FLOWER advances by one: F→G, L→M, O→P, W→X, E→F, R→S. The same +1 shift on GARDEN gives G→H, A→B, R→S, D→E, E→F, N→O = HBSEFO.

mpsc-group-b-ri-2026-p2-B67.expectedQuestion: Liani drove 50 km towards east from a city ‘P’ and then turned right and drove another 30 km. Now she turned to her left and drove another 30 km. mpsc-group-b-ri-2026-p2-B67.explanation: Take P as origin: 50 km east reaches (50, 0); facing east a right turn is south, so 30 km gives (50, -30); from south a left turn is east, so 30 km gives (80, -30); a right turn from east is south again, so Q = (80, -60). Straight-line PQ = sqrt(80^2 + 60^2) = 100 km - the 140 km option is just the total distance walked, not the shortest distance.

mpsc-group-b-ri-2026-p2-B75.expectedQuestion: Statements: I.All apples are bananas II.All bananas are sweet Conclusions: I.Some apples are sweet II.Some bananas are apples

mpsc-group-b-ri-2026-p2-B81.expectedQuestion: How many times in a day the hands of a clock are straight?

mpsc-group-b-ri-2026-p2-B90.expectedQuestion: The following numbers form a series that follows a certain pattern. Find the odd one out. 53, 57, 66, 82, 110, 143, 192

mpsc-group-b-ri-2026-p2-B91.expectedQuestion: A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is shorter than B but taller than E. F is taller than C. Who is the second tallest person?

Working strictly left to right instead gives (39 − 4) ÷ 2 × 3 = 52.5, and answering 6 means stopping after the inner arithmetic.

mpsc-group-b-ri-2026-p2-B94.expectedQuestion: If ‘-’ stands for addition, ‘+’ stands for division, ‘÷’ stands for multiplication, and ‘×’ stands for subtraction, which one of the following equations is correct?

Seven adjacent shaded bars stand over the x-axis labels 125, 130, 135, 140, 145, 150 and 155, each label centred under its bar (so the labels are class marks). The bar heights, written above each bar, are: 125 → 1, 130 → 3, 135 → 2, 140 → 8, 145 → 5, 150 → 4, 155 → 1. Total frequency is 24.
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q71.explanation: Frequencies against class marks are 125→1, 130→3, 135→2, 140→8, 145→5, 150→4, 155→1, so N = 24 and Σfx = 3385, giving mean = 3385/24 = 141.04. Bars strictly above that mean are 145, 150 and 155, i.e. 5 + 4 + 1 = 10 students — note the question asks for students above the average mark, not the number of bars.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q74.expectedQuestion: An 800ml mixture contains water and milk in the ratio 8:2. How much more water and milk should be added in the same mixture to get them in the ratio 9:3?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q74.explanation: The 800 ml holds 640 ml water and 160 ml milk, and the target 9:3 is just 3:1. Adding 80 ml of each gives 720:240 = 3:1 exactly; the other options give 3.04, 2.88 and 2.92, none of which is 3.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q75.expectedQuestion: A 300m long train is running at the speed of 60 km/hr. If it crosses a tunnel in 2 minutes, what is the length of the tunnel?
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q75.explanation: 60 km/hr = 1000 m/min, so in 2 minutes the train covers 2000 m, which equals tunnel + train length. Tunnel = 2000 − 300 = 1700 m.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q77.expectedQuestion:
The central angle subtended by the savings portion on the pie chart is approximately equal to:
A pie chart headed 'EXPENDITURE' divided into four labelled sectors: Food 48%, Rent 26%, Savings 18% and Electricity 8%. The four percentages sum to 100%, and the stated total income is ₹24,000.
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q77.explanation: Savings is 18% of the total, so its central angle = 18% of 360° = 64.8°, which is approximately 65°.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q78.expectedQuestion:
What is the ratio of the expenditure on electricity to that on rent?
A pie chart headed 'EXPENDITURE' divided into four labelled sectors: Food 48%, Rent 26%, Savings 18% and Electricity 8%. The four percentages sum to 100%, and the stated total income is ₹24,000.
mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q78.explanation: Electricity is 8% and rent 26%, so the ratio is 8:26 = 4:13. In rupees that is ₹1,920 : ₹6,240, which reduces to the same 4:13.

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q79.expectedQuestion: There are 12 boys in a class of 20 students. A student is chosen from the class at random to be the class representative. What is the probability that the class representative is a girl?

mpsc-group-b-jao-2026-p2-Q57.expectedQuestion: Among the 10 students of a coaching class, the average weight of 6 students is 56kg. If the average weight of the remaining students is 59kg, then what is the average weight of all students?
